page.layout: One page of handwriting, no printed text. Handwritten lines in brown ink at the top and middle, handwritten shelf and bibliographic notes below, and pencil marks at the bottom left. None of this is printed text.
page.notes: The page carries only manuscript (handwritten) material and no printed text. Per the rules, handwriting is left out of the transcription. The handwritten lines are: "Timor Domini: timor expulit omnem ... " (a Latin proverb-like phrase in a 17th-century hand, partly illegible), "Remissio affert secum ut ... fidem in Deum: ... fides vero admirabilem ..." (a sentence on remission and faith), and bibliographic references such as "Brunet I, 1502" and "Erdmann S. 29." Pencil shelf marks at the bottom left are also not printed text. Because these are handwriting, nothing is transcribed.
